TCN surface exposure ages of glacial landforms in central and northeastern Nevada are generally consistent with the timing of the most recent glacial advance in the region, which is associated with MIS 2 and is likely to be of late Wisconsinan age.
the Ruby-East Humboldt Mountains and the Sierra Nevada were glaciated during MIS 4 and 2, with the former glaciation possibly extending into MIS 3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of boulder ages to date moraines must take into account the potential for underestimates in the ages of older moraine surfaces.

TCN ages of moraine boulders may be used with confidence only if the boulders are sampled from the crest of the moraine, and even then, the ages are likely to underestimate the age of the glaciofluvial advance that formed the moraine.

TCN ages of glacial deposits may be unreliable indicators of the timing of glacial advance if moraines are significantly degraded or if they are sampled in a region that is undergoing active denudation.
